$comment: WHICH MEASURED FIGURES MUST BE ON WHICH PAGE, and this half is the point.
check-measured-figures.mjs on its own only compares figures that ARE marked. That
catches a figure going stale and catches nothing at all if the figure is deleted.
Removing an uncomfortable number from a page would turn the build GREEN, which is
the same defect the check was written to close, pointed the other way.
So coverage is declared here and enforced in both directions:
- a key listed here and absent from its page      -> FAIL, the claim was dropped
- a key marked on a page and absent from here     -> FAIL, an undeclared figure
Adding a row is a deliberate act. Deleting one is too, and it should be argued for
in the commit that does it rather than happening as a side effect of an edit.
The kinds list is now empty because the count is 0, so there is no class name to show and
the declaration's own reason -- 'a count with no class name cannot be acted on' -- no longer
has a subject. Removed in the same commit as the copy change, per the check's instruction that
dropping a measured claim must not be something an edit does quietly.

required.why: The denominator. A percentage without it is a figure nobody can place.
The count of signed records no published version can rebuild. This is the row's whole claim and it is the least comfortable number on the site.
Stated as a proportion as well as a count, because 3,089 reads as small until it is set against 11,432.
WHICH classes. A count with no classes cannot be checked by a reader who holds one of these records and wants to know if theirs is affected.

The resolution records a reader on npm latest cannot check. Now 0, and KEPT AT ZERO rather than dropped: a page that stops citing the figure when it clears cannot show a reader that it ever was not zero. On both pages because the register states the scale and /verify states the cause.
The population the figure was measured over. A coverage claim whose denominator is unstated is unfalsifiable.
A coverage figure is a dated measurement. Both ends of the window are stated so a reader can see what it does not cover.
See above.
The start of the band in which npm latest sits. Without it the reader cannot tell whether the version they hold is affected.
The end of the band. Same reason.
That it was restored is what makes this a withdrawal rather than an absence, and the difference decides what a reader should do about it.
The claim is that latest sits INSIDE the withdrawn band. Naming the band without naming latest leaves the reader to make the comparison the page is asserting.
The version it worked at before the withdrawal. Without it the band reads as 'never shipped' rather than 'taken away'.
How many consecutive releases the gap spans, derived rather than counted by a reader off the two endpoints.
The schema this section derives its field names from. It is the whole provenance claim of section 03; unmarked, it was wrong and nothing could say so.
How many of the documented fields the previously cited schema defines. Zero is the finding.
The denominator. Adding a tenth field block without measuring it would leave this figure quietly wrong.
The size of the placeholder. It is what makes 'defines nothing' concrete rather than rhetorical.
That every other published version defines all of them, which is what makes the citation an error rather than a gap in the schema estate.
The version now cited, derived from which one both defines the fields and validates the artifact.
How many served artifacts pin the vacuous schema. This is the reason the code samples were not changed.
The denominator for the line above.
The commit in which the two verifiers converged. Naming it turns 'they converged' into something a reader can look up.
When convergence landed. The page contradicted its own subject from this date until the correction.
What the hosted service actually runs. The superseded claim that it runs 0.3.3 is exactly the figure that went stale unnoticed.
Stated beside engineRunning because 'agree' is the service's own self-report, and a reader should see the two strings rather than take the boolean.
